reports.title: Preliminary Medical Report
pages:
SUBJECT: Cornelius Pryce, aged 62.
FOUND: Seated at his desk, office of the Sable Flat hangar, 06:10, 18 November 1933. Door bolted from within.

Examination was brief and conducted by lamplight. The subject had a long history of angina and took digitalis drops daily on my prescription. Rigor is advanced; I estimate death between nine and midnight.

PROVISIONAL CAUSE: cardiac failure.

I note, for completeness, an unusual pinkness of the face and hands which I am not able to account for in this light. A full examination should be made by the coroner when the road is open.

— M. L.

reports.title: Background: Vivienne Pryce
pages:
Chief,

Vivienne Pryce, 38, née Vivienne Lark. Played the Belasco and two seasons in London, engaged to Mr. Pryce at the time of the Marigold crash, and quit the stage in 1932 to marry him.

She holds a block of shares in Pryce Transcontinental in her own name. Under the will (as the lawyer's clerk read it to me over the wire) she inherits most of the rest.

Staff say she and Mr. Pryce kept separate rooms this past year. She was polite to everyone at dinner and watched Captain Strand most of the night.

— D. C.

reports.title: Background: Capt. W. Strand
pages:
Chief,

Captain Wilhelmina Strand, 34. Air Mail pilot, barnstormer before that. Crashed a Jenny in 1929 and burned both hands. Flies for Pryce under contract.

She was on the roster to fly the Marigold in May 1931 and refused the flight because of the weather. Mr. Pryce called her a coward in front of the ground crew. Tom Reeve flew in her place. She doesn't talk about it.

She owes money in three states, and Mr. Pryce bought up most of it.

— D. C.

reports.title: Background: Dr. M. Lindqvist
pages:
Chief,

Dr. Matthias Lindqvist, 56. Swedish-born, trained in Uppsala and Zürich. Medical examiner to Pryce Transcontinental since 1928: he signs the pilots' fitness certificates.

He passed Tom Reeve fit to fly the Marigold. Some of the ground crew say Reeve wasn't well that week; nobody says it louder than a mutter.

He keeps a small practice in Tonopah but spends a good deal of time out here for a doctor with no patients.

— D. C.

reports.title: Background: J. Ferreira-Blake
pages:
Chief,

Julian Ferreira-Blake, 41, vice-president of Meridian Air. Meridian lost two Air Mail bids to Pryce in 1931 and has been trying to buy the company ever since.

He came to Sable Flat to close the sale. Miss Quill says he left Mr. Pryce's office at twenty to nine holding a contract that had been torn in half.

He flew in his own Waco, which is parked on the apron.

— D. C.

reports.title: Background: A. 'Ox' Brennan
pages:
Chief,

Abel Brennan, 33, called Ox. Chief mechanic at Sable Flat since 1929. Worked on the Marigold. Goes to church in Tonopah when he can get a ride, keeps racing pigeons, says very little.

He has lived at the airfield year-round since the crash. He asked for no leave in two years. The quartermaster says he does more of the cooking than his job requires.

— D. C.

reports.title: Background: Tamsin Quill
pages:
Chief,

Tamsin Quill, 29, Mr. Pryce's secretary since 1930. Types everything that leaves the office, files everything that comes in, including weather reports.

She said at dinner, in front of everyone, that she 'would not miss him'. Her salary is ordinary. Her clothes are not.

— D. C.

reports.title: The Marigold Accident, 1931: Summary
reports.from: Bureau of Air Commerce (extract), copied by D. Cole
pages:
FORD TRIMOTOR 'MARIGOLD', Pryce Transcontinental Air.
DEPARTED Sable Flat 14 May 1931, 02:40, for the Air Mail connection at Albuquerque.
WEATHER on file: 'clear by noon'.
LOST in a storm over Raven Ridge, 03:17. Six persons aboard. No survivors reported.

FINDINGS: The aircraft flew into high ground in poor visibility. Pilot error in deteriorating weather is the probable cause. Engines and airframe were found serviceable as far as could be determined after the fire.

The investigation was closed in December 1931 at the request of the operator and with the agreement of the insurer.

(Danny's note: 'closed at the request of the operator'. I've never seen that line in a crash summary before, Chief.)

reports.title: Sable Flat: Who Is Here This Weekend
reports.from: Pryce Transcontinental passenger and staff book, copied by D. Cole
pages:
Arrived Thursday 16 Nov: Mrs. V. Pryce (from Los Angeles, by Trimotor). Dr. M. Lindqvist (by road).
Arrived Friday 17 Nov: Mr. J. Ferreira-Blake (own aircraft, Waco). Inspector R. Hart and Agent D. Cole (Air Mail, 17:40, storm closing).
Resident staff: Capt. W. Strand (pilot), Mr. A. Brennan (mechanic), Miss T. Quill (secretary), Mr. W. Hobbs (radio).

Aircraft on the field: Ford Trimotor 'Marigold II' (NC-9930); Waco biplane (Meridian); Air Mail Pitcairn.

No other persons are recorded at Sable Flat.

(Danny's note: ten of us, one storm, nobody leaving. Cosy.)
